newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank PBK workers demand higher wages.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank PBK workers demand higher wages.

text.p: Trade unions at Polish Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), due to be sold in a public offer this year, are demanding higher wages for the bank's lowest earners, a spokeswoman for the bank's Solidarity union said on Thursday.

"During the company's five-year transformation period we did not touch the question of a pay rise. As a result, there has been severe payment differentiation and a decrease in real earnings," Ewa Siemieniak-Bujak told Reuters.

She said that although the average wage in the bank had increased in 1997 in line with earlier agreements, the lowest earning workers, who constitute up to 60 percent of all employees, remained underpaid.

Earlier this week, PBK's trade unions submitted to the treasury minister, PBK's legal owner, a motion for a no-confidence vote against the bank's board. But Siemieniak- Bujak said the unions would not stage a strike.

The bank's spokesman Marek Klucinski told Reuters that the average wage in the bank had increased in the first half of the year by 28.6 percent, or 16.7 percent excluding bonuses, against a 17-percent growth agreed at the start of the year.
Klucinski said the bank's board had informed the trade unions early in July that it planned to address the issue of earnings in October.
Warsaw-based PBK, one of Poland's leading retail banks, plans to go public at the turn of September and October.
The bank's net profit increased to 212.9 million zlotys last year from from 121.1 million in 1995.
